caption: In a dark hallway a fingertip is brought slowly toward a metal doorknob, and a tiny spark jumps from the fingertip to the knob just before they touch.

sa.check: A dark hallway with a metal doorknob.
A fingertip is brought slowly toward the knob.
A tiny spark jumps from the fingertip to the knob just before they touch.
The spark comes as the finger nears the knob, not while it is far away.

pc.expect: The spark is a thin bright line spanning the last small gap between fingertip and knob, appearing when they are almost touching.
pc.fail: The spark appears while the finger is still well away from the knob; or the spark spans from the finger to a place other than the knob; or the spark is a glow on the knob with no line to the finger; or the finger touches the knob and only then a spark appears at a distance.

pc.expect: The spark is a single brief flash and is gone; nothing glows before or after, and the knob is dark once the finger touches it.
pc.fail: The spark glows on between finger and knob for the rest of the clip; or the knob glows before the finger approaches; or sparks flash repeatedly while the finger rests on the knob; or the spark drifts away as a lit point.

pc.expect: The knob and door stay still as the finger approaches; the finger's movement is the only motion.
pc.fail: The knob turns or the door swings as the spark jumps with no hand on it; or the finger is thrown back without the arm moving it; or objects in the hallway shift at the flash.

pc.expect: The spark's light is small: it brightens the fingertip and the knob for an instant and no more.
pc.fail: The whole hallway lights up at the spark as if a lamp came on; or the knob's surroundings stay lit after the spark; or the fingertip glows on.

pc.expect: The finger stops at the knob's surface or touches it; neither passes through the other; the knob stays on the door.
pc.fail: The finger passes into the knob or the door; or the knob detaches and floats; or the door changes shape; or a second hand appears from nowhere.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The door's colour, the knob's finish and the hallway stay the same apart from the flash.
pc.fail: The door changes colour; or the knob changes shape or finish; or the hallway's contents rearrange.

note: The hand is kept because the spark jumps from it; the person is otherwise not judged.
